points.title: Project documentation
points.must: Technical documentation (for programmers / maintenance: algorithms, code, data dictionary, ERD, DFD, test plan) vs user guide (for users: installation, how-to, screenshots, troubleshooting) — readers, contents, language.

points.title: Header and footer
points.must: Definition: areas in the top / bottom margin whose content is automatically repeated on every page (or section).

points.title: Field
points.must: Placeholder filled in and updated automatically: page number, number of pages, date, file name.

points.title: What headers and footers contain
points.must: Title, section name, version and date, logo (header); page number, author, copyright / confidentiality, file name (footer) — with why each is useful.

points.title: Advantages and options
points.must: Typed once, consistent, fields update; different first page, odd/even pages, sections; how to insert (Insert → Header / Footer / Page number).

points.title: Header vs heading
points.must: Header: top margin, repeated on every page; heading: a title in the body text, appears once, used for the TOC.

points.title: Footnote and endnote
points.must: Footnote: note at the bottom of the same page linked to a reference mark; endnote: notes collected at the end of the document or chapter.

points.title: Uses of footnotes
points.must: Citing sources (avoid plagiarism), explaining technical terms, extra detail, cross-references; automatic numbering; References → Insert Footnote.

points.title: Footnotes vs endnotes
points.must: Comparison: position, reading, page layout, best use.

points.title: Table
points.must: Definition: information in rows and columns of cells, easy to read, compare and find; caption = numbered title (Table 4. …).

points.title: Tables in project documents
points.must: Test plan, data dictionary, schedule, requirements, troubleshooting, revision history — with their columns; a test-plan example.

points.title: Good practice for tables
points.must: Header row (bold, repeated on each page), caption, consistent alignment, borders / shading, merge cells, one kind of data per column; why a table beats a paragraph.

points.title: Table of contents
points.must: Definition: list of headings with page numbers at the start; built automatically from heading styles; entries are links.

points.title: Creating and updating a TOC
points.must: Heading 1 / Heading 2 styles → References → Table of Contents → Update Table after editing; automatic vs typed TOC; table of figures / list of tables.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: Typing page / footnote numbers by hand; header vs heading; footnotes for main text; tables without headings or captions; TOC not updated.
